evidence: Manual (Route Assistant desktop, Collector robot, real parent form tree): the Model and Type radio groups' 24x24 circle-and-dot controls sit flush against the left edge of their bordered row, with no left inset, while the retained React Configuration group directly above them (Left/Right) shows the token-specified left padding before its own circles. Two screenshots were provided: one of the current Angular Model/Type sections showing the missing left padding, and one of the Configuration section (and a prior-generation render) showing the padding present.

Source inspection confirms the mechanism: radio-button-group.component.ts's stylesheet declares `.rbg > app-radio-button { padding-inline: var(--rbg-padding-x); }`, but every `<app-radio-button>` element is written inside astronaut-model.component.ts's own template (as content projected into `<app-radio-button-group>`), so under Angular's default ViewEncapsulation.Emulated it carries astronaut-model's `_ngcontent` attribute, not radio-button-group's. The compiled selector requires both the ancestor and the descendant to carry radio-button-group's own scope attribute, so it never matches the projected `<app-radio-button>` elements and the padding rule silently never applies.
visualCriteria.diagnosis: FAIL: a genuine, reproducible visual regression, not a documented styling limitation. RadioButtonGroupComponent's left/right inset for its radio rows depends on a parent-scoped CSS rule targeting projected content, which Angular's emulated view encapsulation never lets match; every current and future consumer of app-radio-button-group nested inside another component's template (as this flow's Model/Type sections are) will render its radios without the intended inline padding. The fix belongs inside RadioButtonComponent's own template/styles (for example moving the padding onto `.rb-row` itself, sourced from a value the group passes down some other way) rather than the group's projected-child selector.
